chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibn Fazzal, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) rejected the testimony of the beggar who begs in his palm.
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Because he is not trusted regarding the testimony, and that is because if he is given, he is pleased, and if he is prevented, he becomes angry.

key_terms.السَّائِل: The beggar / The one who asks

ai.seo_question: Why is the testimony of a beggar rejected in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (AS) elucidates the juristic principle of 'Ghalabat al-Zann' (prevalence of suspicion) by rejecting the testimony of a beggar, whose primary motivation is material sustenance. This ruling highlights the Shia legal emphasis on 'Adalah' (integrity) and the potential for financial need to compromise a witness's impartiality, ensuring judicial fairness by excluding those with conflicting economic interests.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ibn Fazzal, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Hareyz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> rejected the testimony of the beggar, the one who begs by his palm’.
Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Because he is not to be trusted upon the testimony, and that is because if he is given, he is pleased, and if he is prevented, he gets angry’.
en.sarwar: 13. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from ibn Faddal from Hammad ibn ‘Uthaman from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has narrated the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, rejected the testimony of a beggar who extends his hand for help.
It is because he does not believe in testimony in the sense that if one gives to him something he is happy and if he does not give anything he becomes angry.’”
